distribution.narrative: Lin & Beaver (2023: 129) described Craniodicticus cinnamomi from Taiwan based on specimens collected from unhealthy branches and twigs of Cinnamomum insulari-montanum. The holotype male was collected at Ren'ai Township, Nantou County, Taiwan (1,204 m elevation), on 19 November 2022. This original-description evidence supports Taiwan occurrence; no occurrence in mainland China is inferred.

host_note: The original description explicitly reports specimens from unhealthy branches and twigs of Cinnamomum insulari-montanum (Lauraceae). Adults and galleries were observed in the host material; the authors described the species as phloeophagous and harem polygynous (Lin & Beaver, 2023: 129, 131–133).
taxonomy_summary: The current accepted identity is Craniodicticus cinnamomi Lin & Beaver, 2023, described as a new species from Taiwan.

taxonomic_history.name: Craniodicticus cinnamomi
taxonomic_history.note: Described as a new species in Lin & Beaver (2023: 129), with a type locality in Nantou County, Taiwan.

nomenclature_note: The original description published the Chinese name 肉桂異翅擬長小蠹 (Lin & Beaver, 2023: 129); the simplified Chinese display name is 肉桂异翅拟长小蠹. Existing taxonomic backbone identity VSN_1618 is retained.
